messages:
alexa: Heads up — proposal to add a lightweight gating layer for OTel/Prom tags before they hit platform dashboards. Too many high-cardinality labels are drowning the runtime slices.
ben: +1. Can you sketch what "gating layer" means here? runtime vs ingest vs dashboard? :thinking_face:
alexa: Thinking a combination: (1) lint rules at instrument-time (CI), (2) runtime sanitizer that drops or maps tags above cardinality threshold, (3) a dashboard-level allowlist for high-cardinality exploratory fields.
carla: From eng-runtime: we need deterministic mapping rules. If runtime maps model_variant -> mv:quant32, etc, it must be stable or dashboards break.
dino-bot: deploy 1856009900: telemetry-lint v0.2 applied to staging (ruleset proto v3). Logs: 2 dropped labels in /v1/infer for test tenant.
elaine: Can we define a simple naming convention first? e.g., telemetry.label.service, telemetry.label.route, telemetry.tag.model_family, telemetry.tag.model_variant. That helps both OTel and Prom label translation.
ben: Agreed on names. Also propose we reserve prefix high_card_ for fields allowed to be cardinality-heavy but only surfaced in debug workspaces.
frank: Ops concern: if we silently drop tags at runtime we'll break legacy alerts. Need a rollout plan: default passthrough in beta, warn mode, then enforce with automatic mapping.
alexa: Rollout plan idea: 1) lint + warnings in CI and console (2) runtime sanitizer in warn-mode for 2 weeks (3) enforce with metrics mapping + export rules and doc updates. Add a canary that only applies to 10% of traffic.
carla: For mapping rules, propose a canonicalize map file in repo: metrics/label_mappings.yaml. Example:
```
- match: model_variant
  map_to: model_variant
  strategy: collapse_prefix
  keep_top_k: 20
```
That gives runtime deterministic behavior.
dino-bot: note: metrics/label_mappings.yaml updated in branch metrics-gatekeepers. CI lint results: 7 warnings for route names, 0 errors.
elaine: Dashboards: we should create a "cardinality playground" dashboard that queries raw OTel traces (retention short) for exploratory analysis. Only infra/devops role can view it.
ben: Also need a signal to alert when new label keys appear frequently — make a low-volume daily report to #eng-platform with top new keys.
frank: How do we handle user-provided metadata that could be explosive (e.g., prompt_id)? Should be dropped by default and allowed via explicit opt-in per-tenant.
alexa: Yes. Default deny for unbounded user metadata. Add policy: user_metadata.* -> drop unless tenant-config allows `allow_user_metadata: true`.
carla: Implementation note: runtime can use an LRU set per tag_key to track distinct values and apply keep_top_k. That keeps memory bounded.
dino-bot: test results: keep_top_k=50 on staging reduced cardinality spike by 82% for a synthetic load.
elaine: Docs task assigned: @elaine to draft naming conventions + rollout checklist. Ben to own the alert/report. Carla to implement mapping loader in runtime. Alexa to own gating policy doc and canary plan.
ben: Sounds good. Quick question — do we want to adopt `telemetry.tag.*` vs `telemetry.label.*`? Pick one and stick with it.
alexa: Let's standardize on `telemetry.label.*` for anything that becomes a Prom label and `telemetry.tag.*` as a synonym in logs only. Document mapping.
frank: I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk owners through the canary steps.
alexa: Thanks everyone — I'll open the top-level RFC and link the mapping proto/CI rules. Expect the RFC in the next hour.
carla: Thanks — will review RFC and try to get an initial mapping loader PR up by EOD.
ben: Ping me on PRs. :thumbsup:
